You are a code worker editing the freytag-forge repo. Your current working directory IS a git worktree of /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge. Edit files ONLY under the current working directory; NEVER edit anything under /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge directly (you may only run its .venv/bin/python). Do NOT git commit, do NOT git add -A, do NOT touch .git, do NOT edit any file under storygame/ or data/.

OWNED FILES (create these, edit nothing else): tests/test_design_review_fixtures.py, and (only if you need shared helpers) nothing else. Write your notes (Part A verdicts: one line per claim formatted '1. HOLDS ...' through '5. ...', plus assumptions) to /home/bcorfman/dev/ringer-work/design-review-step1-notes/notes.md instead (create the directory) so it survives the worktree.

BACKGROUND: a design review (read .plans/chatgpt-design-review-answer.md, sections 1-4, and .plans/design-review-implementation.md 'Step 1') found that the offline tests use one fully-earned late state per scene and only check that formerly accepted narration stays accepted. Step 1 adds six small STATE-EXACT regression fixtures that build the real engine state at a specific point (not a fully-earned substitute) and assert behaviour with no network and no model calls. Read tests/test_narration_corpus.py first for house style (RuntimeState.bootstrap, RuntimeEngine(state, provider).turn(...), ProposalValidationError with .code, load_story_package of data/stories/continuity-initiative). Also read tests/test_knowledge_projection.py, tests/test_candidate_matcher.py, tests/test_cue_spent_reveal.py and tests/test_narration_term_traps.py for how projection, matching, cues and term guards are exercised.

PART A, VERIFY THESE CLAIMS AGAINST THE CODE (read-only; report each as HOLDS or FAILS with file:line in notes.md): (1) models.py validates a pacing field nudge_after_turns but engine.py cue scheduling never reads it; (2) engine.py excludes a cue from scheduling once its id is in delivered_cue_ids and never re-delivers it; (3) knowledge.py candidate projection keeps only 4 candidates by default while cloudflare.py semantic fallback caps at 6; (4) the 40-call semantic counter in cloudflare.py lives on the provider instance and web_demo.py builds a new provider per request; (5) matcher in candidate_matcher.py returns nothing when two candidates tie. If a claim FAILS, say so and adapt the matching fixture to the real behaviour.

PART B, SIX FIXTURES in tests/test_design_review_fixtures.py, one test function each (name each with the case), each docstring naming the review finding it pins (Finding 1 name guards, 2 recovery, 3 reveal matching, 4 measurement):
 1. ordinary_name_accepted: at an EARLY state of a scene (use bootstrap + scene entry only, do not assert earned knowledge), narration that uses an ordinary public name for a thing declared in that scene is accepted ('ok'). Find a real example in the story package (a declared item or place in the scene whose name is not secret).
 2. premature_secret_rejected: at an early state, narration that names a protected term whose reveal has NOT been earned is REJECTED with the specific error code the engine raises (use real data; pick a term from a knowledge item's protected/leak terms or an unrevealed later-scene name; assert the exact code via error.code, look at tests/_rejection_codes.py). This is a must-reject entry.
 3. skipped_reveal: a state where the player is in a later scene but an earlier reveal was never earned (do not assert its establishes facts); assert the guard on that reveal's protected term still rejects the term, i.e. the guard does not lapse just because the scene moved on. If current behaviour differs, assert the CURRENT behaviour and put a comment 'CURRENT DEFECT (review Finding 1): ...' explaining.
 4. missed_pointer: a cue is delivered once and the player ignores it for several turns, with the reveal still eligible and unearned; assert the cue is NOT delivered again (current behaviour, review Finding 2), with comment 'CURRENT DEFECT (review Finding 2): no escalation; nudge_after_turns unused'. Drive it through the real engine turn loop or the engine's cue-scheduling function, with a stub provider.
 5. matcher_tie: two eligible candidates whose evidence groups both match one player input: assert the matcher returns no match (current behaviour, review Finding 3). Use real package candidates if a real tie exists, else two synthetic ActionEvidenceCandidate objects built with the dataclass fields.
 6. more_than_four_eligible: a state with more than four simultaneously eligible reveals in one scene (find the scene by scanning the package with the engine's eligibility helper explain_reveal or the projection code); assert projection keeps four and that a fifth, correctly matching candidate is dropped from the projected list (current behaviour, review Finding 3). If no real scene has more than four eligible at once, build the state by asserting required facts for a scene with the most reveals, and say so in notes.md.
Each test must build state with RuntimeState.bootstrap(PACKAGE), set current_scene_id and phase like tests/test_narration_corpus.py does, and assert only the facts that point needs. Use module-level PACKAGE loaded once. Keep tests fast (whole file under 10 s) and hermetic (no network, no env vars, no live worker). Do not mark anything xfail: assert present behaviour and name the defect in a comment, so the suite stays green now and a future fix must update the test deliberately. Player input strings must be imperative commands in the player's voice (e.g. 'Search the drawer.', 'Open my laptop.'), never first person narration, no non-events like 'Wait.'.

HOW TO RUN: first confirm `PYTHONPATH=$PWD /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -c "import storygame; print(storygame.__file__)"` prints a path inside the cwd. Tests: PYTHONPATH=$PWD TMPDIR=/tmp /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_design_review_fixtures.py then the whole suite with -n auto. Ruff: PYTHONPATH=$PWD /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m ruff check --fix . and -m ruff format . . Finish by replying with the files changed and the Part A results.
tasks.check: bash -c 'set -u; N=/home/bcorfman/dev/ringer-work/design-review-step1-notes/notes.md; [ -s $N ] || { echo FAIL no notes at $N; exit 1; }; for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do grep -qiE "(^|[^0-9])$i[).:].*(HOLDS|FAILS)|claim $i.*(HOLDS|FAILS)" $N || { echo "FAIL notes lack verdict for claim $i"; exit 1; }; done; git add -A -- tests/test_design_review_fixtures.py; bad=$(git status --porcelain | grep -v "tests/test_design_review_fixtures.py" || true); [ -z "$bad" ] || { echo "FAIL stray files:"; echo "$bad"; exit 1; }; OUT=/home/bcorfman/dev/ringer-work/design-review-step1-patches; mkdir -p $OUT; git diff --cached > $OUT/step1.patch; [ -s $OUT/step1.patch ] || { echo FAIL empty patch; exit 1; }; for t in ordinary_name_accepted premature_secret_rejected skipped_reveal missed_pointer matcher_tie more_than_four_eligible; do grep -q "def test_.*$t" tests/test_design_review_fixtures.py || { echo "FAIL missing test $t"; exit 1; }; done; grep -q "xfail" tests/test_design_review_fixtures.py && { echo FAIL xfail used; exit 1; }; PYTHONPATH=$PWD TMPDIR=/tmp /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_design_review_fixtures.py 2>&1 | tail -15; [ ${PIPESTATUS[0]} -eq 0 ] || { echo FAIL fixtures; exit 1; }; PYTHONPATH=$PWD TMPDIR=/tmp /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider -n auto 2>&1 | tail -8; [ ${PIPESTATUS[0]} -eq 0 ] || { echo FAIL full suite; exit 1; }; /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m ruff check . && /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m ruff format --check . || exit 1; echo PASS'
